A_target.statement:
Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]] and $H \subseteq S$.
Then the [[Definition:Closure (Topology)|closure]] of $H$ is:
:$\displaystyle H^- = \bigcap \set {K \subseteq S: H \subseteq K, K \text { closed} }$
and is the smallest [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed set]] containing $H$.

B_source.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Group|group]] and $S \subseteq G$.
Then the [[Definition:Generated Subgroup|subgroup generated by]] $S$ is:
:$\displaystyle \gen S = \bigcap \set {H \le G: S \subseteq H}$

substitutions.the family of subgroups containing S: the family of closed sets containing S

validity_conditions: The defining class (subgroups / closed sets) is closed under arbitrary intersection, so the intersection of all members containing S is again in the class.
That intersection contains S and is contained in every member, hence is the smallest such object.
The argument is identical in both settings; only the word 'subgroup' vs 'closed set' changes (a closure-operator pattern).
proof_plan:
Let $\KK$ be the family of all [[Definition:Closed Set (Topology)|closed sets]] containing $H$ (respectively, all [[Definition:Subgroup|subgroups]] containing $S$).
$\KK$ is non-empty as $S \in \KK$ (respectively $G \in \KK$).
From [[Intersection of Closed Sets is Closed]] (respectively [[Intersection of Subgroups is Subgroup]]), $\bigcap \KK$ is again closed (respectively a subgroup).

$H \subseteq \bigcap \KK$, and $\bigcap \KK \subseteq K$ for every $K \in \KK$.
Hence $\bigcap \KK$ is the [[Definition:Smallest Element|smallest]] element of $\KK$.

Thus $\bigcap \KK$ is the [[Definition:Closure (Topology)|closure]] $H^-$ (respectively the generated subgroup $\gen S$).
{{qed}}
